heading: Mission
text: The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) promotes the adoption of secure cloud services across the US Government by providing a standardized approach to security and risk assessment.

heading: Vision
text: Accelerating the expansion of a marketplace of secure cloud services for the Federal Government

heading: Framing
text: Federal Security policy requires all systems to be authorized based on risk.

heading: Framing
text: FedRAMP standardizes the process for cloud, providing:

heading: DO ONCE, USE MANY TIMES
text: Doing security authorizations right the first time allows agencies to re-use work and eliminate duplicative efforts

heading: TRANSPARENCY
text: Increased collaboration and creation of a community among the US Government and vendors that did not exist before, establishing the first government-wide FISMA program

heading: VALIDATED WORK
text: FedRAMP validates security authorizations to ensure that there is uniformity among security packages

heading: CENTRAL SHARING
text: Centralized repository where agencies can request access to security packages for expedient authorizations

heading: FISMA
text: Federal Information Security Modernization Act requires agencies to protect Federal Information. FISMA requires NIST to develop standards and guidelines

heading: OMB A-130
text: OMB states that when agencies implement FISMA, they must use NIST standards and guidelines

heading: FedRAMP Policy
text: FedRAMP leverages NIST standards and guidelines to provide standardized security requirements for cloud services; a conformity assessment program; standardized authorization packages and contract language; a repository for authorization packages

heading: FedRAMP Authorization Act
text: FedRAMP Authorization Act establishes a Government-wide program that provides a standardized, reusable approach to security assessment and authorization for cloud computing products and services that process unclassified information used by agencies.

heading: Framing
text: There are two paths to an authorization, through the JAB or Agency

heading: Joint Authorization Board Provisional Authority to Operate (P-ATO)
text: The primary governance and decision making body for the FedRAMP program

heading: Joint Authorization Board Provisional Authority to Operate (P-ATO)
text: CIOs of DoD, DHS, and GSA strictly review CSP packages for an acceptable risk posture using a standard baseline approach

heading: Joint Authorization Board Provisional Authority to Operate (P-ATO)
text: The JAB issues provisional authorizations (P-ATO); this is not a risk acceptance, but an assurance to Agencies that the risk posture of the system has been reviewed by DoD, DHS, and GSA, and approved. Each Agency must review and issue their own ATO that covers their Agency's use of the cloud service.

heading: Agency Authority to Operate (ATO)
text: Agency Initial ATO: Initial Agency reviews CSP FedRAMP security package; Agency/CSP submits the security package and Agency ATO to the FedRAMP PMO. FedRAMP confirms package meets FedRAMP requirements and makes security package available for Agencies to reuse.

heading: Agency Authority to Operate (ATO)
text: Agency Leveraged ATO: Agency reviews JAB or Initial Agency FedRAMP ATO security packages and issues Agency ATO. Agency sends a copy of ATO letter to FedRAMP PMO for record keeping.
